title: The hospital accordion player who has been busking for 35 years

input.lead: Volunteer John Jones, 84, has been entertaining patients and visitors with his musical talents
input.summary: Volunteer John Jones, 84, has been entertaining patients and visitors with his musical talents
input.evidence_text: The hospital accordion player who has been busking for 35 years - BBC News Image source, East Cheshire NHS Trust Image caption, John Jones taught himself to play the accordion after his father passed away By Mairead Smyth , North West and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 1 hour ago For 35 years, volunteer John Jones has been entertaining patients and visitors at Macclesfield District General Hospital by playing the accordion. The 84-year-old retired engineer discovered his love of the accordion as a child, watching his father play the instrument. "My dad played the accordion all the time and I could play the piano a little bit," he said. "When he died, I started messing around with his accordion. "One half is like a piano, but the other half is completely different with buttons. "I had to teach myself, but I really enjoyed it." He has since been using his musical talents to raise money for East Cheshire NHS Charity. John's volunteering began after visiting the hospital with his mother-in-law in 1991 where he saw an appeal for a CT scanner. He has since raised hundreds of thousands of pounds for the charity. "One of the nicest moments was about five years after helping to raise the money for the scanner, I had to have a CT scan myself," said John who has an MBE for services to charity. "The nurse said, 'That's ironic, you're using the scanner you helped pay for.' That really stayed with me." 'It's a privilege' The money has been used to fund a family room at the hospital intensive care unit, where his wife June died from sepsis in 2020. "She'd been in intensive care five years earlier with sepsis as well, but she managed to survive that one," said John, who also performs in care homes. Officers from Greater Manchester Police (GMP) were called to Market Street at 19:00 GMT on Tuesday. title: Manchester City Council says e-scooter trial could begin in 2027

input.lead: The scheme could be up and running by summer 2027 if approved, the council says
input.summary: The scheme could be up and running by summer 2027 if approved, the council says
input.evidence_text: Manchester City Council says e-scooter trial could begin in 2027 - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, Manchester City Council said the scheme could be up and running next summer By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 28 October 2026 People in Manchester could be travelling around on a fleet of electric scooters next year after plans for a new trial were announced. Manchester City Council is putting together proposals for the scheme and said in a report that it could begin in summer 2027, although the authority added it had not yet considered an operator for the e-scooters. The plans come off the back of the Lime scooter scheme in Salford which Salford Council said had been a major success. A council spokesperson stressed that a decision on whether to proceed with an e-scooter trial had not yet been made, and was conditional on backing from Greater Manchester Police and other groups. Image source, LDRS Image caption, E-scooters were launched in Salford in September 2020 They said provisional approval had been received from the Department for Transport (DfT) for the council to develop a proposal, and "officers are currently undertaking work to assess future benefits, risks and how an e-scooter scheme could work in practice in Manchester". Summer 2027 was the latest a trial could start in line with DfT requirements for new trials, they added. The council's report on e-scooters said they could offer Manchester residents and visitors a "popular zero-emission transport mode" to get around the city. An e-scooter trial was launched in Salford in 2020 and the city has continued to renew the scheme every two years since then, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. title: Bury Market gets £10m government funding boost in Budget

input.summary: The £10m Bury Market investment programme was included in Chancellor John Healey's Budget
input.evidence_text: Bury Market gets £10m government funding boost in Budget - BBC News Image caption, The £10m Bury regeneration investment scheme featured in Chancellor John Healey's first Budget By Georgie Docker North West Published 28 October 2026 The government will contribute a further £10m towards the restoration of Bury town centre, Chancellor John Healey has announced during his first Budget. The money will be invested in the Bury Market project as part of the government's Growth Mission Fund. More than £33m has so far been invested in the Greater Manchester town's market area, including a £20m grant from the Conservative government in 2024 . "Securing this funding has taken sustained work by the council - with the support of MP James Frith's campaigning in parliament," said Bury councillor Charlotte Morris. "It's a fantastic result for Bury - Bury Market is the jewel in our town centre's crown." Image caption, Bury's Indoor Market Hall closed in October 2023 Bury Council said the latest funding announcement would build on the town's long-term regeneration plans and address the former Indoor Market Hall's condition and enable its future use. The Indoor Market Hall closed in October 2023 following the discovery of reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete (RAAC). Since then, new outdoor market canopies have been erected and a new food, drink and events venue is due to open in November. title: Children at council-run home illegally tattooed each other

input.lead: The children had tattooed themselves and others using illegally bought kit, Ofsted found
input.summary: The children had tattooed themselves and others using illegally bought kit, Ofsted found
input.evidence_text: Children at council-run home illegally tattooed each other - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Inspectors found staff at the home in Salford had "failed to act" when a child repeatedly tattooed themselves, other children in the home, and "reportedly peers in the community" By Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 28 October 2026 Young people at a council-owned children's home were found to have tattooed themselves and others with illegally bought kit, a government watchdog found. An Ofsted inspector discovered staff at the home in Salford had "failed to act" when a child repeatedly tattooed themselves, other children in the home, and "reportedly peers in the community". The home was rated 'inadequate' by Ofsted and handed three compliance notices to improve children's safety and welfare. A Salford City Council spokesperson said: "We accepted the findings of the inspection in full and have already taken swift action to address the issues raised, resulting in recent positive feedback from Ofsted." "Children now have multiple permanent tattoos which may impact their future choices and opportunities," the inspector wrote in their report. "And children did not receive appropriate medical support and remained exposed to potential health risks." The report also found that staff applied consequences "punitively", with children's bus fares regularly withheld, including for travel to family contact. Inspectors described the practice as "excessive and unreasonable" and noted the type of punishment "does not promote children's welfare or relationships with their families". title: Bolton Council to consider national changes to planning system - Bolton Council

input.lead: Bolton Council will hold a meeting on November 10 to consider national changes to the planning system
input.summary: Bolton Council will hold a meeting on November 10 to consider national changes to the planning system
input.evidence_text: Bolton Council to consider national changes to planning system – Bolton Council Published: Wednesday, 28th Oct 2026 Bolton Council will hold a meeting on November 10 to consider national changes to the planning system. What are the changes? Last year, the government updated the National Scheme of Delegation for planning applications. Under the changes, which come into effect on October 31, more applications would be decided by planning officers rather than by a committee of elected members. The government has said this would make planning applications quicker, more efficient and reduce the number of decisions overturned on appeal. Larger and more contentious applications would still need approval from planning committees. What happens next? For these changes to be implemented in Bolton, there must first be an amendment to the council constitution agreed by a vote at Full Council. At a meeting on October 7, Full Council voted against amending the constitution to incorporate the new National Scheme of Delegation. The matter will next be considered by Full Council on November 10. How will this impact my planning application? Nationally the new rules will apply from October 31. This means Bolton Council will not legally be allowed to hold Planning Committee Meetings or determine any planning applications, after this date unless and until the constitution is amended. The council will continue to receive and assess new and existing applications during this period. Unfortunately disruption to the planning system locally and delays to decisions are inevitable. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. title: Bolton Car Boot Sale

input.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
input.summary: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
